name: Tanhá

anatomy.part: enamel point, left side of crown
pulp chamber, the living nerve at the centre of the tooth
right edge of the pulp chamber
root canal running down the right root

myth: Tavo the Gale was once out over the Windward cliffs in a fury, because a kite-line had been stiff with salt and would not bend for him. He bit it. He bit it hard, and his tooth came out in his jaw and went up. Tavo laughed, because that is what he does, and the wind howled with him. Then the tooth stuck in the Unflown, where things lost go, and it has stayed there ever since, white and cold, with the rope still in it. Ennu the Kite-Wright says it could be fetched. Hesk says a thing that has been counted cannot be uncounted. Aun, who would try anything, once went south to take it back. He came home with a bloody hand and no tooth, and he did not say what he had seen, only that the tooth was smiling. So if you find yourself with a stiff line in a gale, do not bite it. Mend it with your hands.
verse:
Tavo laughed and bit
a rope too hard, the tooth stayed
still up in the dark
